g.text: Reconciling a file with the server (--abs-pull, --abs-pull-only, --abs-push)
the whole reason the reconciliation below is two
lines rather than a rule of its own. By commit
time the merged list is what the file context
holds, so asking it what the file had returns
what the merge just put there.
pull - match this file to a book,
says which of the two it was
no book matched, or the match
the merge has settled a list
Write unless the marks came from the file and are
unchanged; send unless they came from the server
The equality test here is stricter than the one
the merge note uses. The note asks "are these the
same marks", where a differing title is noise;
this asks "is there anything left to do", where
it is not. It converges: once written, the file's
own list is what the next probe returns.
write the marks into the file
Sent as complete: this path forms no opinion
about chapter numbers at all, so it cannot be
holding a partial sequence back the way a
detection run that failed to close a gap is.
--abs-sync is a spelling, not a sixth mode: it sets
